claim_text: An outside party got into Tower Records Online without authorisation on Nov 19, and customer data was taken
summary: Tower Records Japan's own notice says it confirmed unauthorised access from outside on the online shop at about 5:10 PM JST on Nov 19, took the service offline, and later confirmed that customers' personal information leaked.
detail: Nikkei, Investing.com, NHK, Asahi, Sankei, Yomiuri, Bloomberg (via The Japan Times), FNN and Kyodo News (via Okinawa Times) report the same, all relaying the company's notice, so for sourcing they count as one source behind the company's own statement. None of them says how the access happened or who was behind it.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's own notice (Tier 1) states the unauthorised access and the leak; nine outlets repeat it.

claim_text: The company took the online shop offline for emergency maintenance after spotting the access at about 5:10 PM JST on Nov 19
summary: After confirming the access around 17:10 Japan time on Thursday Nov 19, the notice says, Tower Records stopped the service for emergency maintenance. It is still stopped for safety checks.
detail: Nikkei says the shop was accessed 'on the afternoon of the 19th' and that the stopped service is delaying orders already placed. Investing.com calls Nov 19 the day the intrusion was 'detected'. The notice gives the time as 'about' 17:10. Kyodo News gives the same date but not the time.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The notice gives the date and approximate time; Nikkei, Investing.com and Kyodo News give the same date.

claim_text: About 11 million records of customer personal information leaked, including people who left the membership within three years
summary: The notice puts the total at about 11 million records and says it covers Tower Records members, including customers who cancelled their membership within the past three years. Nikkei repeats the 'about 11 million' figure.
detail: The notice then gives three counts, one per set of information (c004 to c006). They are 10,214,652, 2,784,514 and 776,953, and they add up to more than 11 million. The company does not say how the counts overlap or how the 11 million is reached, so treat 'about 11 million' as the company's headline figure.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's notice states the figure and who is covered; Nikkei relays both. Kyodo News relays only the headline figure.

claim_text: 10,214,652 login records leaked: email address, member ID and a hashed password
summary: The notice lists 10,214,652 'login information' records containing the email address, the member ID and the password hash.
detail: The notice explains a hash cannot be read back into the original password on its own. Investing.com rounds this to about 10.2 million accounts and says email addresses and user IDs were exposed. The company does not say which hashing method was used.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The notice's table gives the count and the fields; Investing.com repeats the rounded count.

claim_text: 2,784,514 member profile records leaked: name, name reading, nickname, birth date, sex and postcode
summary: The notice lists 2,784,514 'member information' records with name, furigana (the reading of the name), nickname, date of birth, sex and postal code.
detail: Nikkei's shorter summary says members' email addresses, names and addresses were included. In the notice, addresses are in the shipping set (c006), not this one.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The notice's table gives the count and the fields; Nikkei gives a shorter version.

claim_text: 776,953 shipping records leaked: address, addressee name and phone number
summary: The notice lists 776,953 'delivery destination' records with the address, the name on the parcel and a phone number.
detail: This is the smallest of the three sets and the only one the notice says holds phone numbers. Yomiuri rounds it to about 780,000.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The notice's table gives the count and the fields; Yomiuri repeats the rounded count.

claim_text: Tower Records says no credit card information was included
summary: The notice says credit card information is not among the leaked items. Nikkei repeats that card information and similar data were not included.
detail: This is the company's own statement about what its investigation found. Nikkei, Asahi, Sankei and Yomiuri relay it, so it is one source. No outside check has been published.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The notice states it in a footnote to the data table; four outlets repeat it.

claim_text: No harm from the leak was known as of Nov 21, per the company, which warns of fake emails
summary: The notice says no secondary harm had been found as of Saturday Nov 21. It warns of suspicious emails posing as the company and asks customers not to open links or attachments.
detail: The notice also asks customers not to enter personal information, passwords or card details in response to such messages. Nikkei repeats the 'no secondary harm reported as of the 21st' line. This is a snapshot from the company, not a finding that none will occur.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Both give the company's own statement as of Nov 21; it cannot be checked from outside.

claim_text: Orders: online-shop orders start shipping from Mon Nov 23 JST; marketplace seller orders have no restart date
summary: The Nov 22 notice update says online-shop orders will start shipping in turn from Monday Nov 23. Marketplace orders have no restart date while the seller management site is still being checked.
detail: Event orders for new releases the week of Nov 23 were handed to the carrier before the shutdown and arrive as planned. These are plans, not completed events. Nikkei says the stopped service is affecting shipping of orders already placed, and Yomiuri says some ordered items appear not to have shipped. On Nov 23 JST, FNN (Fuji TV) relayed the plan that shipping restarts in turn from that day; the company had not yet posted that shipping had begun when we checked.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The notice's shipping update states the plan; Nikkei and Yomiuri report the shipping delay. FNN relays the Nov 23 restart plan.

summary: Tower Records has not said how the access happened. The notice says only that outside access was confirmed, that checks and investigation continue, and that results will be posted on its site.
detail: Investing.com says the company did not disclose how attackers gained access. No technical write-up, vulnerability or third-party supplier has been named in the sources we read, including the Nov 22 reports from NHK, Asahi, Sankei and Yomiuri.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The notice and Investing.com both leave out the method.

claim_text: Who is behind the Tower Records breach
summary: No attacker, group or claim of responsibility has been named by the company or the outlets we read.
detail: None of the Nov 22 reports from NHK, Asahi, Sankei or Yomiuri names one either. We did not look for claims on leak sites or forums, and cite such claims only if reported by press.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: None of the three sources names an attacker.

claim_text: Whether this breach is linked to other Japanese retailer data incidents reported this week
summary: Investing.com and Bloomberg (via The Japan Times) mention a separate incident at another online retailer and a second retailer on the same marketing platform. Neither says Tower Records used that platform.
detail: Bloomberg places Tower Records' disclosure after the other retailer's, as context. No source we read links the Tower Records access to it.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Investing.com and Bloomberg mention the other incidents as context only and draw no link.
